name: Art Deco
summary: Stepped towers, zigzag and chevron relief, and rich materials in a symmetric frame. It came from the Paris exhibition of 1925 and made the skyscraper and the cinema into the pictures of the machine age.

philosophy.core_thesis: Modern technology deserves luxury: the machine age should look glamorous, symmetric and expensive.
design_principles: Step the silhouette back in setbacks of 1.5 to 4m as the tower rises, and end it with a spire, a crown or a lantern.
Stress the vertical: run piers or fins unbroken from the base to the crown, with spandrels recessed 100 to 300mm behind them.
Compose the front on one central axis and balance both sides; the entrance is the richest point.
Use geometric ornament: zigzag, chevron, sunburst, fluting and stylised flora in low relief of 25 to 75mm.
Mix rich and industrial materials: polished stone, chrome, aluminium, bronze and glass in one elevation.
Give the lobby the most ornament of the building: a tall hall with a patterned floor, metal doors and a lit ceiling.
anti_patterns: Smooth undecorated planes with no relief
Curved, whiplash or plant-like line work
Raw concrete or visible formwork marks
Asymmetric, informal composition with no axis
A flat-topped box with no crown or setback

massing.form: A stepped, setback tower or a symmetric block with a strong central mass and lower wings.
massing.proportion: Tall and slender: a tower of 1:4 to 1:8 plan to height; low cinemas and hotels use a 1:1.5 front with a central vertical sign.
massing.roof: A crown of stepped tiers, a spire or a lit lantern; flat parapets carry relief or finials.
massing.relation_to_ground: A tall polished base of stone or metal, 1 to 2 storeys, with a grand entrance of 5 to 8m height.

structure.system: A steel frame clad in stone, terracotta or brick; reinforced concrete for cinemas and exhibition halls.
structure.span_and_module: A tight vertical module of 1.5 to 2.5m between piers; column grids of 6 to 9m inside.
structure.expression: The frame is hidden. The vertical piers express the lift of the tower, but they are cladding and not structure.

materials.finish: Polished and lustrous: metal gleams, stone is honed, and each surface is machine-cut with sharp edges.

facade.composition: A symmetric front of tall piers and recessed spandrels, with one central ornamental panel above the entrance.
facade.openings: Narrow vertical windows between the piers, with metal spandrel panels; the window-to-wall ratio is 30 to 45%.
facade.solid_to_void: Solid leads: 55–70% opaque, in strong vertical stripes.

light_and_space.daylight: Daylight is moderate; the lobby is lit by indirect cove light and metal lamps, so it glows at night.
light_and_space.spatial_sequence: A grand axis from the door to the lift hall: vestibule, then a tall lobby, then a ceremonial stair or lift bank.
light_and_space.interior_character: Patterned terrazzo or marble floors, metal grilles, lacquered panels and lighting fixtures designed with the building.

ornament.attitude: Ornament is geometric, repeated and machine-made; it celebrates speed, light and luxury.

rules.rule: Hold the front on one axis with a stepped central mass.
Repeat piers and zigzag bands in a strict vertical beat.
Step the massing back in setbacks toward the crown.
Use vertical piers to lift the eye to the spire.
Build the lobby with a double height and a rich finish.

emotion.target_response: Glamour and ambition: the viewer feels a confident city of speed, wealth and progress.

avoid_when: The brief asks for a quiet, domestic or low-cost building.
The design needs a free plan or an informal, asymmetric composition.

modifiers.how: Remove the relief and the setbacks, flatten the piers into a grid of 4 to 7m, and keep the polished materials.

sources.title: Bevis Hillier, Art Deco of the 20s and 30s (Studio Vista, 1968)
